Task: Classify land cover types
Classify land cover types in Myanmar using a decision tree applied to a Landsat image collection from 1991 to 2017. It uses a pre-defined classification structure with eight classes, including Forest, Rubber, Palmoil, and Urban areas, and applies temporal filtering and majority voting (mode) over a 7-year window to reduce noise. The classification is based on pixel values from composite images, with masking by high-probability pixels (threshold >95) from a probability dataset. The output is a time-series of annual land cover maps exported as assets, each representing discrete land cover classes with associated colors and legend display on the map.

Task: Identify burned areas using BAI and TBR
Identify burned areas in a forested region using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from May 2019. It applies cloud masking, masks water and non-forest areas using MNDWI and ALOS PALSAR forest/non-forest data, computes NDVI and MNDWI, then calculates the Burn Area Index (BAI) and a custom spectral index called TBR (Transformed Burn Ratio). A dual-threshold method is applied on BAI and TBR to detect burned pixels. The output is a time-series mosaic of burned area detections across seven overlapping weekly intervals, combined into a final classified raster map highlighting burned regions with red color, and exported to Google Drive as a GeoTIFF.

Task: Monitor agricultural vegetation change
Analyze temporal changes in agricultural vegetation in Godda district using Sentinel-1 VH polarization SAR data from June to September in 2021 and 2022. It computes mean VH backscatter across multiple time windows, stacks them into a multi-temporal raster, and clips the result to the district boundary. Additionally, it processes Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from October 2021 and 2022 to generate false-color composites (B8, B4, B3) for visual interpretation of land cover. Outputs include two stacked SAR image composites (2021 and 2022), two optical mosaics (2021 and 2022), and their visualization layers on the map for comparative analysis of seasonal vegetation dynamics.

It constructs a multi-temporal stack of VH band means, trains a Random Forest classifier on labeled ground truth points for paddy and other land covers, applies the classification, refines results by masking non-paddy classes and small disconnected regions, and generates a final binary paddy map. Outputs include a classified raster, accuracy assessment (confusion matrix and overall accuracy), and exported area statistics and maps for validation and further analysis.

Task: Identify rice cultivation area

Task: Generate median composite image
Create a cloud-masked median composite image from Landsat 7 Surface Reflectance data collected between 2000 and 2021. It applies pixel_qa-based cloud masking, filters images by cloud cover (<40%), selects specific spectral bands, computes the median value per pixel across the time series, clips to a user-defined region (table), and visualizes/exports the resulting mosaic as a true-color image.

Task: Classify cropland areas using Sentinel-1 time series
Classify land cover types in Bihar, India, using a time series of Sentinel-1 VH polarization SAR imagery from June to August 2022. It applies temporal filtering, speckle reduction via the refined Lee filter, and Random Forest classification trained on user-provided labels (e.g., krice3–6, other) to generate a land cover map. The output includes a classified raster with masked urban/barren areas using WorldCover, accuracy assessment (confusion matrix and overall accuracy), area calculation per class in square meters, and exports of both the classification and filtered backscatter stack.

Task: Classify aridity and climate zones
Compute a high-resolution, rule-based climate classification system using CHELSA v2.1 (1981–2010) bioclimatic variables. It derives annual precipitation (P_ann), potential evapotranspiration (PET_ann), and the Aridity Index (AI = P_ann/PET_ann); identifies seasonal precipitation regimes (HS_ratio: Apr–Sep share); applies latitude-based monsoon/Mediterranean rules; incorporates thermal controls via hottest and coldest monthly temperatures to define cold-condition classes (e.g., cold ocean → class 7, cold land → class 9); and finally combines three orthogonal dimensions — coldness class (0–9, ×100), aridity/climate class (0–9, ×10), and summer heat class (0–9) — into a unique 3-digit integer 'combined' code (e.g., 492, 515). The output is a discrete raster map of these combined climate codes clipped to a user-specified U.S. state (e.g., Montana), visualized with a custom color palette for interpretation.

Task: Classify aridity and climate regimes
Compute a high-resolution, rule-based climate classification map using CHELSA v2.1 (1981–2010) bioclimatic variables. It derives annual precipitation (P_ann), high-sun season precipitation (P_hs, Apr–Sep), mean potential evapotranspiration (PET_ann), and the UNEP aridity index (AI = P_ann / PET_ann). It combines AI thresholds with seasonal precipitation distribution (HS_ratio), latitude zones (tropics, north/south subtropics), and thermal extremes (hottestC and coldestC) to assign base aridity classes (Humid → Arid Desert), then overlays monsoon/Mediterranean seasonality rules and cold-climate overrides (e.g., cold ocean → class 7, cold land → class 9). Finally, it fuses thermal seasonality — summer intensity (via hottestC) and cold-season severity (via coldestC) — into a three-digit combined code (coldClass×100 + climateClass×10 + summerClass), producing a discrete, interpretable climate regime raster. The output is a clipped, palette-colored classification layer for a user-specified U.S. state (e.g., 'North Dakota').

It computes vegetation indices (NDVI, EVI, SAVI, OSAVI, SATVI, NDWI), applies Fmask-based cloud/shadow/snow masking, and harmonizes Landsat 8 OLI data to be consistent with earlier sensors using Roy et al. regression coefficients. A CCDC (Continuous Change Detection and Classification) algorithm is applied on the NDVI time series to detect breakpoints and magnitude of change. the workflow identifies mangrove gain, loss, degradation, and regeneration by combining classification masks (e.g., Giri mangrove extent, user-defined 2020 classification) with NDVI anomaly thresholds and temporal break analysis. Outputs include spatial maps of gain/loss timing and magnitude, annual area change statistics, and charts showing yearly trends in mangrove change.

Task: Assess vegetation and water health
the workflow assesses temporal vegetation and water health in coastal Bangladesh using Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery (2000–2024). It computes NDVI (B5/B4), NDWI (B3/B5), and an illustrative SPI (B2−B3); extracts annual maximum values over the ROI; generates time-series charts for NDVI and NDWI; and applies threshold-based classification to categorize pixels into 'Healthy', 'Moderate', or 'Unhealthy' for both vegetation (using NDVI thresholds: ≥0.6, ≥0.4, <0.4) and water (using NDWI thresholds: ≥0.3, ≥0.1, <0.1). Outputs include interactive time-series charts, max-value statistics, and classified image collections — all spatially constrained to Manikganj district (used as proxy for coastal districts despite comment mismatch), with no final raster export or area quantification implemented.

Task: Classify land cover types
Classify land cover in the Baía region using Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance imagery from January 2019 to January 2020. It applies a cloud and shadow masking function (maskL8sr) using pixel_qa bits and band thresholds, computes a median composite, clips to a user-defined feature collection, and performs Random Forest classification trained on labeled regions (vegetation, rural properties, anthropogenic, water, exposed). The output includes a classified raster map with five classes, an accuracy assessment (confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and Kappa), NDVI visualization, and area calculation in square kilometers. The final classified map is exported to Google Drive and Earth Engine Asset, along with the clipped composite.

Task: Identify maximum confidence gain class

Task: Compute NDMI from Landsat
Compute the Normalized Difference Moisture Index (NDMI) using near-infrared (SR_B5) and shortwave infrared (SR_B6) bands from a cloud-masked, median-composited Landsat 8 surface reflectance image collected between February and March 2023. It calculates NDMI as (NIR - SWIR) / (NIR + SWIR), clips the result to the AOI, visualizes it with a red-white-green palette, and exports the continuous NDMI raster to Google Drive at 30m resolution.

Task: Analyze vegetation and surface moisture conditions
Analyze vegetation health and surface moisture conditions using Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS imagery from June 2015 over a defined AOI in Central Europe. It computes EVI (Enhanced Vegetation Index) and Tasseled Cap Wetness (TC_WET) and Brightness (TC_BRT) indices through spectral transformations. Key steps include cloud masking, radiometric calibration, atmospheric correction via scaled reflectance, and median compositing. Outputs include calibrated RGB, VEG (vegetation-enhanced), HV (shortwave infrared-enhanced) visualizations, EVI, TC_WET, and TC_BRT rasters, which are displayed on the map and printed for inspection.

Task: Analyze historical NDVI patterns
Analyze historical vegetation conditions in a specified field (lote) using NDVI derived from Sentinel-2 imagery between 2015 and 2018. It applies cloud filtering, computes NDVI, filters images by NDVI threshold (>0.2), and calculates temporal percentiles (10th and 90th) to define dynamic visualization bounds. A time-series slider panel is created to visualize individual NDVI images with adaptive contrast, and a composite mean NDVI image is classified into clusters using K-means. The final output includes a mapped historical NDVI layer, interactive time-series visualization, clustered vegetation zones, and export of the NDVI composite to Google Drive.
